story.overview: Clean up tool call summaries and sandbox output to provide professional, noise-free status messages to users. Users should see meaningful status updates without technical artifacts like Python imports, stack traces, or debug statements.
story.user-story: As a user, I want tool call summaries and code execution outputs to be clean and professional, so that I see meaningful status updates without technical noise like Python imports or stack traces.
story.background:
This story addresses three related problems: 1. Tool Summary Standardization: Define consistent formats for what users see during tool execution 2. Sandbox Output Filtering: Filter out Python imports, debug output, and technical noise from user-facing responses 3. Error Message Cleanup: Convert technical errors into user-friendly messages
Pain points include: code leakage (import pandas as pd shown in status), raw stdout visible, stack traces in error messages, and inconsistent status message formats.

acceptance-criteria.criterion: AC1: No Code Leakage in User-Facing Output - Python import statements, module loading messages, and internal code MUST NOT appear in user-facing messages when PTC code execution produces stdout/stderr output.

AC2: Filtered Sandbox Output - Filter out: lines starting with 'import' or 'from ... import', Python REPL artifacts ('>>> '), stack traces starting with 'Traceback', file reference lines ('File "/'), empty/whitespace-only lines normalized, debug statements (DEBUG:, [DEBUG], VERBOSE:, [VERBOSE]).

AC3: Consistent Tool Summary Format - Use standardized format: '{Action} {Tool Name} - "{context}"'. Examples: 'Searching MSCI Reports - "Hulu Q3 revenue"', 'Executing code - generating Excel report'.

AC4: User-Friendly Error Messages - Convert technical errors to friendly messages: ModuleNotFoundError -> "The requested operation requires a capability that isn't available", TimeoutError -> "This operation took too long", PermissionError -> "I don't have access to that resource", ConnectionError/HTTPError -> "Couldn't connect to the external service", Unknown -> "Something went wrong. I'll try a different approach."
AC5: Status Message Guidelines Documented - Clear guidelines in project-context.md covering standard format, allowed vs. forbidden content, examples for common tool types.

AC6: Test Coverage for Filtering - Unit tests verify filtering for: single import, block imports, mixed output, stack traces, debug statements, REPL artifacts, whitespace normalization, edge cases (empty, null, whitespace-only), multiline imports.

technical-notes.note: ESM Import Extension - Always use '.js' extension in imports: import { x } from './module.js'
Tool Handler Pattern - Every tool handler MUST wrap its body in try/catch and return ToolResult, never throw
Slack mrkdwn Format - Use *bold* not **bold**, use <url|text> not [text](url)
Logging - Include traceId in every log entry, use logger.* methods not console.log
Test Organization - Co-located tests: *.test.ts alongside source files

relevant-sections.section: Code execution via code_execution_20250825 tool type. Container reuse via containerLifecycle by threadTs. Skills loaded via buildContainerParameter(skillIds). All betas consolidated in config.anthropic.allBetas. Output filtering should occur after receiving code execution result, before displaying to user.

Dynamic status messages via setStatus with loading_messages array. Status should reflect current tool being called. Use formatToolSummary() for consistent formatting. Error messages should be contextual with suggested actions.

Layered errors: InternalError (logged) -> ToolError (to Claude) -> UserError (to Slack). Tool handlers return ToolResult with success/error, never throw. Log technical details with traceId, show friendly message to user.
All handlers wrapped in startActiveObservation(). Span naming: {component}.{operation}. Include traceId in every log entry. Log technical error details before humanizing for user.

patterns-to-follow.pattern: Always use .js extension in relative imports
Return { success: true, data } or { success: false, error } - never throw
Include traceId in every log, use logger.* not console.log
Use branded types where possible (ToolName, ErrorCode, MemoryPath)

anti-patterns.anti-pattern: Show raw stdout to users - Filter through sanitizeCodeOutput()
Display stack traces - Use humanizeError() for user message
Ad-hoc status strings - Use formatToolSummary() consistently
Log user-friendly errors - Log technical details, show friendly to user
Filter too aggressively - Preserve meaningful output (results, summaries)
Import without .js extension - Always use .js for relative imports
console.log for logging - Use logger.* methods with traceId
